newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Turkish premier meets Nigeria's Abacha on trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish premier meets Nigeria's Abacha on trade.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, under attack at home and abroad over his visits to pariah nations, on Tuesday met Nigeria's military leader General Sani Abacha.
"The discussions were cordial as relations between the two countries are good," a foreign ministry official said.
Nigeria is the Islamist premier's last stop on a tour that has outraged a large section of both the Turkish public and the NATO country's traditional western allies.
Erbakan flew into Nigeria on Monday after visiting Egypt and another pariah state, Libya.
Nigeria, Africa's most populous nation, is an international outcast because of its human rights record and the failure of its military government to ensure a swift return to civilian rule.

United States Secretary of State Warren Christopher on Monday sought support from the Commonwealth and European Union for sanctions on Nigeria, as he began a continental tour which will not bring him near Abuja.
Limited sanctions were imposed by western countries in November when Nigeria hanged nine minority rights activists, including author Ken Saro-Wiwa, for murder.
The Commonwealth of Britain and its former colonies last month pulled back from imposing proposed sanctions to give Nigeria a chance for dialogue.
Christopher did not elaborate on possible measures, but U.S. officials said there was no chance of an embargo on crude oil sales that account for 95 percent of Nigeria's export earnings.
Oil and gas is one of the areas in which Nigeria and Turkey are looking for greater collaboration.

Annual trade between the two countries is worth barely more than $1 million, but Turkey has said it will take $100 million of liquified natural gas, when a plant under construction comes on stream in 1999.
"This session will afford both parties the opportunity to examine this matter in greater detail," a foreign ministry statement said.
Erbakan brought with him four government ministers who on Monday discussed a draft protocol on the Nigerian-Turkish joint commission with industry minister Mohammed Hailadu, officials said.
"We expect something to be signed before the delegation leaves," a foreign ministry official said.
A delegation of about 200 businessmen including chief executives of some of Turkey's largest companies also accompanied the prime minister.

Apart from oil and gas cooperation between Turkey and Nigeria, the visit is expected to focus on commerce and tourism, construction, agriculture, banking, health, free trade zones, transportation and telecommunications.
A Turkish left-wing party on Tuesday said it had requested a parliamentary censure motion to topple Erbakan.
The opposition and Turkish media have attacked him for his weekend visit to Libya during which Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi strongly criticised Turkey's treatment of its Kurds and its western ties.
